183	## Proposed implementation owners and acceptance
184	
185	| Responsibility | Owning target modules | Required evidence |
186	|---|---|---|
187	| Common projection, data validation and offline assembly | Reporting projection/html_embedding/assets; report report-data and generated binding | Applicable parity, hostile text, unknown/incompatible payloads, no network fetches, required failure propagation |
188	| Overview, historical selection and catalogs | Report overview-view, history-view and catalog-view; host query/configuration | Exact IDs and history scope, missing evidence states, admissible catalog provenance |
189	| Findings, evidence and audit | Report findings-view, evidence-view and comparison-view | Complete required fields, baseline attribution, runtime/import limitations and honest incomplete results |
190	| Graph and symbol exploration | Report graph-view and symbol-detail-view; host query and reporting projection | Exact occurrence identities, bounded relationship/path results, no client-derived policy or global absence claim |
191	| Navigation, help and exports | Report navigation, help-view and exports | Keyboard/focus behavior, safe routes/schemes, formula-safe local download, no analysis or mutation effects |
192	| Publication and optional opening | Host delivery and platform process/filesystem | Atomic artifact output, correct after-commit failures, no launch in disallowed contexts |
193	
194	These browser modules are additions to the canonical filename inventory, not
195	new applications or providers. Sorting, fuzzy search and layout can be browser
196	presentation functions over embedded data. Any browser-computed subset statistic
197	must be labelled as such; semantic paths, completeness, verdicts and required
198	parity values come from the host projection. No client-side operation can obtain
199	new repository evidence or promote a display result to an authoritative finding.
200	
201	## Explicit migration boundaries
202	
203	- The prototype includes heuristic browser tracing and body-hash lookups. Their
204	  useful navigation is retained through exact identities and host evidence, not
205	  by reproducing those algorithms as authoritative analysis.
206	- The old shared graph filter drawer is not a retained feature: its source says
207	  it was removed ([filters.ts](https://github.com/opensip-ai/opensip-cli/blob/a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0/packages/dashboard/src/client/filters.ts)). Current visualization owns its controls; other views use their
208	  own filters. The surviving hidden test exclusion is explicitly removed by R07/R08. Avoid restoring obsolete UI based on filenames alone.
209	- A report is an offline snapshot. Its availability observations describe the
210	  recorded observation time/generation; opening the file tomorrow does not learn
211	  whether the live store was purged. Fresh availability requires a new admitted
212	  host query/report, with explicit identity and observation provenance.
213	- HTML is advertised by exactly `default`, `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`,
214	  `candidates`, `inspect`, `review-brief` and `repair-preview`. Graph/history
215	  data reach those reports through embedded host projections. `query` advertises
216	  only human/JSON/agent output; it does not gain HTML from browser navigation.
217	  SARIF is advertised only by `default`, `analyze`, `audit` and `repair-verify`.
218	  The embedded projection/schema mapping must follow those exact applicability
219	  sets before UI implementation. These feature rows do not add arbitrary
220	  fields to closed CommandEnvelope schemas or advertise a new report command.
221	- Graph display budgets, browser limits and package-size targets need measured
222	  acceptance thresholds. Do not inherit the prototype’s 8 MiB graph budget or
223	  its history caps as product law. They are useful cases for the measurement plan.
224	- Visual styling, frontend framework, graph library and exact legacy simulation
225	  UI remain separate choices. R24 preserves generic selected-result presentation
226	  and records that no separate simulation capability is selected; it cannot
227	  remove a capability or waive required parity.

233	degradation cannot conceal a required output failure. Assess local editor-link
234	privacy and the distinction between offline evidence navigation and live queries.

# Typed metadata successor

Candidate for actual Claude review, not an accepted design replacement. This
folder makes the RF-01 proposal concrete while retaining every accepted parent.
The schemas, command inventory, coverage routing and this contract are selected
as one unit. Product implementation must bind their eventual review/assent before
emitting envelope4. The existing planning source-manifest pointer in the coverage
copy remains the base provenance; successor.json supplies this scoped overlay.

CommandEnvelope4 preserves envelope3 payload constraints on the existing branches,
with its own major changed and `meta` forbidden outside `kind=meta`. Metadata
success accepts only schemaFamily, schemaMajor, kind, requestId,
clientCorrelationId, termination, exitCode and meta. Its termination is exactly
`{"class":"success"}` and exitCode0. Failures keep the existing failure carrier,
D9 legality, registered detail and exit-code derivation. No success metadata may
accompany a failure. A major3 reader rejects4, and a major4 reader rejects3.
The evaluator, Run, finding, query and mutation schema identities stay unchanged.

One additional compatibility correction handles ordinary parser refusals. Envelope3
requires a nonempty errors array of registered domain details, yet the registry has
no general unknown-option/topic detail. Envelope4 permits an empty errors array
only when kind=failure, termination is exactly {class:request-rejected,
errorCode:REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION}, exitCode=2, and diagnostics is nonempty. It
cannot carry a run or a metadata success payload. Other empty-error envelopes
remain invalid. Non-applicable format requests continue to carry their existing
OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE detail. No public detail vocabulary or D9 code is
added; a parser error must not masquerade as a configuration or schema failure.

Metadata schema1 has two closed public variants and a private BuildMetadataV1
definition. All schema integer values use the same exact JSON lexical rules as
the accepted foundation. Host releases use SemVer syntax, at most128 Unicode
scalars. Closure IDs use the existing closure2 grammar, at most256 entries in
strict unique UTF-8 order. Development metadata requires an empty list. Release
shape validity alone does not prove assembly admission or qualification.

The help topic is null or a canonical command name; each command row contains
name, usage and summary. Rows are strictly unique by name and UTF-8 sorted.
Semantic admission compares the entire rows to a trusted, build-selected catalogue:
null topic returns the complete catalogue, otherwise exactly its named row. During
implementation that catalogue lists only implemented commands; full product
completion requires all45 selected inventory commands. A known but unimplemented
topic is refused. Aliases resolve to canonical names before projection. Unknown
options/topics use REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION, exit2, and a bounded diagnostic. The
registry has no general command-argument detail: no new detail is invented. The
additional envelope4 correction above makes that existing D9 error deliverable.

Human output renders the same topic, names, usage and summaries. Version output
renders hostRelease, buildChannel and closureIds from the same compiled record.
The fixed declarative metadata selectors are:

| Parity field | Selector |
|---|---|
| command-names | $.meta.commands[*].name |
| host-release | $.meta.hostRelease |
| build-channel | $.meta.buildChannel |
| closure-ids | $.meta.closureIds |

These are fixed selections in the renderer; no arbitrary JSONPath engine is
required. Existing queryDispatch JSON Pointer behavior is unchanged. Completion
remains human-only and shell-specific; an explicit JSON request is the existing
OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE request rejection. Its error delivery follows the
existing command output policy; it does not gain a success metadata variant.

The private build record excludes the host digest/closure, its own digest,
enclosing archives and signing outputs. The accepted planning phrase
"build-embedded signed release descriptor" is corrected within this scope to
"build-embedded metadata covered by the enclosing signed host/release artifact".
Release tooling admits the non-host component closures first, compiles their
selected identities into the host, then the existing release signing/installation
owners bind the finished host bytes. Version describes the shipped selection,
not installed state, current trust, provider health or a fresh signature check.
This introduces no new signature envelope, signatureVerified field or trust path.

M1 must build development metadata from the exact package version with no closure
IDs. There is no environment flag or caller JSON switch to produce a release
channel in M1. Enabling a release path later requires the owning M6 assembly's
actual prerequisite checks and refusal tests. Trusted build selection is an input
to semantic reference checks, not something established by the reference schema.

Bootstrap metadata paths use arguments and compiled constants only. They do not
inspect the project, configuration, providers, store, installation registry,
network or report assets. Operational request/correlation IDs remain metadata.
The bootstrap and delivery still obey existing outcome and I/O failure rules.

check_metadata.py checks exact source pins, schema shapes, compatibility, metadata
semantics and fixtures. It is architecture reference validation. It does not
satisfy future product startup, renderer parity or release qualification tests.

The compiled metadata producer is `crates/reporting/src/assets.rs`, the existing
HostAssetPinV1 constant owner. M1 defines one compiled development-channel constant
there. Both BuildMetadataV1 and any fixture HostAssetPinV1 take their channel from
that one constant, never a separate environment/configuration setting. The M1
metadata constructor produces no closures and takes hostRelease solely from the
CLI's `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` compiled value via bootstrap and host outcomes.
`crates/reporting/tests/projection_tests.rs` owns producer and channel-agreement
negatives; `apps/cli/tests/startup_tests.rs` verifies the exact CLI version and
refusal/ineffectiveness of caller/environment release switches. If an explicit
asset pin disagrees with the compiled selection, its build admission refuses.
Version uses only compiled constants; it does not read assets or their manifest.
No new product file is needed for this producer. M6 may replace the development-
only constructor with its separately reviewed admitted release selection, but
only after the existing assembly prerequisites and refusal checks are executable.
Whether a release can have an empty non-host closure set is decided by that
assembly's required component inventory; shape alone does not authorize a release.

For fixed selector interpretation, `$.meta.commands[*].name` means JSON Pointer
`/meta/commands` followed by a name projection of each row, preserving array order.
The other three selectors are direct `/meta/hostRelease`, `/meta/buildChannel` and
`/meta/closureIds` pointers. No arbitrary selector evaluation is permitted.

The reference checker preserves ExactValidator across all explicit2020-12
resources by retaining their dialect as Resource metadata and omitting only
`$schema` from their validation projection. Otherwise jsonschema4.25.1.evolve
selects the standard validator on an external root reference and silently loses
custom exact-constant/enum/ordering checks. Complete original schema bytes stay
pinned and unchanged. Schema-only external-reference tests now detect this
loss; semantic catalogue/build comparisons cannot mask it. This is a scoped
reference-adapter correction, not a rewrite or requalification of historical
reference evidence.

"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
are the supported alternative.

---

## 8. Command inventory, outputs and parity (AR-13 surfaces, AR-16)

`workflows/command-inventory.v3.json` is the single intended inventory,
validated by `workflows/schemas/evaluator3/command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.

| Group | Commands |
|---|---|
| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
| mutation | `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `repair apply`, `repair recover`, `purge` |
| execution | `test run`, `native prepare` (both explicitly authorized) |
| lifecycle / serve / meta | `install`, `update`, `core update|repair|rollback`, trust/store commands, `doctor`, `agent serve`, `help`, `version`, `completion` |

Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.

**Renderers.** `human` v1, `json` v3 (the `CommandEnvelope` major 3 is the parity
reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and
`retention-disclosure`; inventory admission refuses an omission. SARIF results
and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are
human/JSON/HTML/agent values; no renderer reads an undeclared findings field or

# Report projection contract: `workflows:evaluator3:report-projection:1`

**Standing:** author candidate that closes AUDIT-G10 (P-5, UQ-1). It is for root and fresh independent review, and it is not approval. It changes no product, architecture or existing approval; source45 and prior approvals remain historical. Every parent is pinned byte-unchanged in `successor.json`. Nothing here is measured performance, browser qualification or release qualification.

## 1. Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `report-projection.schema.json` | Complete closed owner schema. Proposed path `docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/schemas/evaluator3/report-projection.schema.json`. |
| `contract.md` | This contract. It holds the admission joins, limits, the 24-row map and the measurement plan. |
| `fixtures.json` | Positive bases, 79 expected-code cases, the feature/view maps, measurement samples and obligations. Generated byte-identically by `build_fixtures.py` from the pinned witness corpus. |
| `check.py` | Reference admission and check. Run `/tmp/opensip-implementation/metadata-reference-env/bin/python -I -B check.py --architecture ARCH [--out check-result.json]`. |
| `successor.json` | Parent and candidate pins, plus two chapter-14 passage overrides. Parents are unchanged. |

## 2. Owner decisions

- **Identity.** `$id urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:evaluator3:report-projection:1`, `schemaFamily opensip.product.report-projection`, `schemaMajor 1`. The family string follows the existing `opensip.product.*` spelling rather than the P-5 sketch's `opensip.report-projection`.
- **Parity.** `envelope` is the complete `command-envelope:4` value and the **only** parity source. Its closed schema is untouched: check.py asserts `additionalProperties:false` and that no exploration member exists. The embedded value equals what the json renderer emits, with two differences only: `agentHints` is always absent, and `projectRoot` appears only under `pathDisclosure.mode=local-editor-links`. Neither is a parity field. Renderers read parity only at inventory4 `parityPaths` or fixed selectors. A panel never restates or overrides a parity value, so join keys are non-parity identities (`coverageId`, `comparisonResultId`, `planId`, owner `resolvedView.runId`).
- **Deltas from the P-5 sketch, all routine design choices:**
  - Every *applicable* panel is **required** as a state, and every non-applicable panel is forbidden. Absence therefore cannot be silent.
  - A history row is `{runId, run: AnalysisResult, findings, findingsProjection}`, not a nested CommandEnvelope. Nesting an envelope would force an invented historical `requestId`, termination and exit code.
  - Graph data is `{request, response}` pairs, so query context (endpoint, relation, direction, depth, view digests) is never lost.
  - Repair-preview recipe display reads the envelope directly and needs no catalog panel.
- **Asset binding.** The raw SHA-256 of the exact schema bytes is the `ReportAssetManifestV1.projectionSchemaSha256s` member. `check.py` prints it; any edit changes it.

## 3. Root document

| Member | Rule |
|---|---|
| `command` | Exactly the inventory4 html set: `default analyze fit audit candidates inspect review-brief repair-preview`. check.py derives it from inventory4 and the prototype inventory. `query`, `repair-verify` and every other command are refused, and no command or format is advertised. |
| `renderer` | `{format:"html", version:1}`, equal to the inventory4 html renderer row. |
| `envelope.kind` | Analysis commands: `run` or `failure`. Query commands: `query` or `failure`, with `querySurface` equal to the inventory4 `queryDispatch.surface`. `meta`, `mutation`, `invocation` and `doctor` are refused. |
| `supportedReportViews` | Required, and the exact per-command constant (§4). |
| `budgetProfile` | `BudgetProfileV1`: all constants (§8). |
| `reportObservedAt` | Host wall-clock time of the projection. Availability and history describe this observation only; it is not trusted time or identity. |
| `pathDisclosure` | `relative-only` (default; forbids `envelope.projectRoot`) or `local-editor-links` with `editorScheme ∈ {vscode, vscode-insiders, idea}`. |
| `panels` | Closed `{evidence, graph, comparison, history, catalog}` of state wrappers. |

## 4. Views and panel applicability per command

| Command | supportedReportViews | Required panels (all others forbidden) |
|---|---|---|
| default | overview, findings, evidence, catalog, graph, symbol-detail | evidence, graph, catalog |
| analyze | overview, findings, evidence, comparison, catalog, graph, symbol-detail | evidence, graph, comparison, catalog |
| audit | overview, findings, evidence, comparison, history, catalog, graph, symbol-detail | all five |
| fit | overview, evidence, catalog, graph, symbol-detail | evidence, graph, catalog |
| candidates | overview, candidate-list, graph, symbol-detail | graph |
| inspect | overview, candidate-inspection, graph, symbol-detail | graph |
| review-brief | overview, review-brief, graph, symbol-detail | graph |
| repair-preview | overview, repair-preview, catalog | none |

Where each view gets its data:

| View | Data source |
|---|---|
| overview | `envelope` run, termination, exitCode, availability, retentionDisclosure and errors; `reportObservedAt` |
| findings | `envelope.findings` |
| candidate-list, candidate-inspection, review-brief, repair-preview | The matching `envelope.queryRecord` record |
| evidence | `panels.evidence` and `envelope.availability` |
| comparison | `panels.comparison` joined to `envelope.run` |
| history | `panels.history` |
| catalog | `panels.catalog`; for repair-preview, `envelope.queryRecord.plan.descriptor.recipe`/`recipeTrust` instead |
| graph | `panels.graph` and `budgetProfile.browserLimits` |
| symbol-detail | Graph endpoints, with findings shown separately (§9, R11) |

check.py asserts every view is used and every source pointer resolves. Help, navigation and exports are presentation behaviour, not data views.

## 5. Panel states and the three limit layers

A panel is `{state:"present", data}` or `PanelNotPresentV1`:

| State | Reasons | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `omitted` | `not-selected`, `exploration-budget-exceeded` | The host did not project it. |
| `unavailable` | `no-admitted-result`, `no-run-identity`, `evidence-expired`, `evidence-purged`, `evidence-missing`, `source-refused` (requires `detail`) | The source could not supply it. |
| `corrupt` | `retained-bytes-corrupt` | Retained bytes exist but cannot be admitted. |
| `incompatible` | `retained-schema-major-unsupported` | Retained data uses an unsupported schema major. |

Catalog `rules` and `capabilities` sections use the same wrapper. Whole-document shape or compatibility failure in the browser is a `report-data.ts` display error, never a degraded panel.

The three limit layers never merge:

1. **Source analysis.** Owner fields stay inside the exact owner records: graph `context.traversalCoverage`, `countBasis`, `truncated`, `totalItems` and `evidence` (coverageIds, scopeIds, deficiencyCitations, resolutionLimitations), plus native `coverage`, `resolutionCompleteness`, `closedWorld` and `deficiency`.
2. **Host projection.** `ItemProjectionV1 {total, omitted, omissionCause}` for prefix-limited lists, `GraphSlotV1.hostProjection.continuation`, and panel `omitted` states.
3. **Browser limits.** `budgetProfile.browserLimits`. Applying one is `view-state.ts` presentation state with a visible disclosure. It never alters data, counts or completeness.

A blank coupling cell, a missing path or an empty table is shown with its layer disclosures, never as a global absence proof.

## 6. Admission joins (check.py `admit`, stable refusal codes)

Order: report-profile codec (`CODEC-DEPTH`, document bytes), exact schema (`SCHEMA`), then the joins below.

**Subject Run anchor.** The anchor is a concrete run3 or none; latest and snapshot views never resolve.

| Envelope | Anchor |
|---|---|
| `kind=run`, authoritative | `run.runId` |
| `kind=run`, ephemeral | none |
| candidates | `queryRecord.context.resolvedView.runId`, only if that view is `{runId}` |
| inspect | `inspection.runId` |
| review-brief | `brief.runId` |
| repair-preview, failure | none |

| Code | Rule |
|---|---|
| J-RENDERER | Command row formats contain html, its requestClass is html-applicable, and `renderer` equals the inventory row. |
| J-EXIT | `exitCode` is the fixed derivation of `termination.class`. |
| J-SURFACE | `querySurface` equals inventory4 `queryDispatch.surface`. |
| J-FAILURE-PANELS | On `kind=failure`, every panel is not-present with reason `no-admitted-result` (the schema already forbids `present`). |
| J-STATE-REASON | `no-admitted-result` only on failure. `no-run-identity` only for graph or history, and only when there is no anchor. |
| J-NOT-SELECTED | `not-selected` only for comparison, and only when `run.comparisonResultId` is absent. |
| J-COMPARISON-ID | Present comparison `comparisonResultId` equals `run.comparisonResultId`. With no selected comparison, the panel is exactly `omitted/not-selected`. |
| J-COMPARISON-RUN | `descriptor.currentRunId` equals `run.runId`. |
| J-ANCHOR | A present graph or history panel requires an anchor. |
| J-GRAPH-RUN | Each response `context.resolvedView.runId` and request `view.runId` equal the anchor. |
| J-GRAPH-PROJECT | Request `projectId` equals response `projectId` equals `envelope.projectId`. |
| J-GRAPH-OPERATION / PAGE | Request and response operation are equal (the schema also fixes them per purpose to graph.* only), and `items` ≤ `page.size`. |
| J-GRAPH-CONTINUATION | `not-embedded` iff `context.nextCursor` is present. The report never follows a cursor. |
| J-GRAPH-VIEWS | Explicit request `factViewDigests` equal the response's. |
| J-GRAPH-RELATION / ENDPOINT | Neighbor rows carry the requested relation and touch the requested endpoint on the requested direction side. Path rows start and end at the requested endpoints with `hopCount ≤ maxDepth`. Reach rows have `depth ≤ maxDepth`, and a depth-0 row exists only with `includeStart:true` and equals the start. |
| J-GRAPH-COUPLING | package-coupling rows are package→package (the request endpoint kind is schema-fixed). |
| J-EVIDENCE-COVERAGE | Envelope `kind=run` and `run.coverageId` equals `data.coverageId`. |
| J-EVIDENCE-COUNTS / J-HISTORY-COUNTS | `total = embedded + omitted`; `item-limit` iff `omitted > 0`; `item-limit` implies embedded = profile limit. |
| J-EVIDENCE-KEYS | Coverage keys are unique. |
| J-HISTORY-SELECTION | Rows map one-to-one to `requestedRunIds`, in order; nothing is substituted. |
| J-HISTORY-RUN | A present row's `run.runId` equals its `runId`. |
| J-HISTORY-CURRENT | The current anchor is never history. |
| J-HISTORY-BASELINE | `selection.baselineId` equals comparison `descriptor.baselineId`. |
| J-CATALOG-PLAN | Rules `source.planId` equals `envelope.run.planId`. |
| J-CATALOG-RULES | Every envelope finding `ruleId` is a listed rule. |
| J-CATALOG-DIGEST | `registrySha256` is the raw SHA-256 of the exact-codec canonical `declarations`. |
| J-BUDGET-ORDER | A panel omitted for budget implies no earlier panel in `budgetOmissionOrder` is present. |
| J-BUDGET-BYTES | Canonical envelope ≤ `envelopeMaxCanonicalBytes`; canonical panels ≤ `explorationMaxCanonicalBytes`; document ≤ `documentMaxCanonicalBytes`. |

Joins that need data outside the document are host obligations under existing owners: the coverage stream behind `coverageId`, the baseline `descriptor.runId`, and that the effective policy is the one the Plan bound. The host must hold these before projecting; the browser does not re-derive them.

## 7. Catalog translation and provenance

The catalog is a new private host display projection.

- **Rules** are exact `policy-document:2 Rule` records from the Run Plan's effective policy, with `source {kind:"run-plan-effective-policy", planId, policyDigest}` and `gateSeverityAtLeast`.
- **Capabilities** are the exact `ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1`, with a report-local `registrySha256`.
- **Descriptions.** There is no free-text description field: no admitted description owner exists, and the component-manifest `displayName` schemas are `CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED`. Views show ids, severity, gate, enablement, subject enumeration selectors, message codes and language modes.
- **No permission.** A row confers no execution, grant or selection permission, and the browser offers no action on it.
- **Recipes.** Repair-preview recipe rows are the envelope's `RecipeRef` and `recipeTrust`. No recipe description or parameter catalogue owner exists.
- **Statistics.** Historical run statistics have no owner and are not shown.

## 8. Budget profile (UQ-1): development limits, not measured performance

| Constant | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| explorationMaxCanonicalBytes | 4194304 | Accepted exact codec `MAX_BYTES` (canonical.py and trial `exact-json.ts`). |
| maxGraphItemsPerSlot | 1000 | graph-query:3 `Bounds.maxPageSize`. |
| maxGraphSlots | 6 | floor(4194304 / (1000 × 635)), using a 635-byte constructed GraphNeighborRow. |
| maxEvidenceEntries | 3956 | floor(4194304 / 1060), using the 1060-byte CoverageResultV3 witness. |
| maxHistoryRuns | 1 | The only selected history source (audit baseline source Run). |
| maxHistoryFindingsPerRun | 5526 | floor(4194304 / 759), using a 759-byte constructed realistic FindingSurface. |
| maxCatalogRules / maxCapabilityDeclarations | 512 / 128 | Owner maxItems. |
| envelopeMaxCanonicalBytes | 83886080 | 100000 envelope4 findings × 759 B, rounded up to a 16 MiB multiple. |
| documentMaxCanonicalBytes | 88145920 | Envelope ceiling + exploration ceiling + 65536 root allowance. |

I wrote the complete report-projection owner for AUDIT-G10 as an author candidate for root and fresh independent review, not approval. The reference check passes on the final files: all 20 pins verify and all 79 test cases give their exact expected result. Nothing in the architecture repo was edited, and no UI or product code was built or run.

**Files** in `/tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-report-projection-author-01`:
- **`report-projection.schema.json`**: the new schema, `$id …:evaluator3:report-projection:1`. Its raw SHA-256 (`02bc8b1b…1811`) is the value that goes into `projectionSchemaSha256s`.
- **`contract.md`**: the rules the schema can't express, limits, the R01–R24 map and the measurement plan.
- **`fixtures.json`**: test documents built from the witness corpus. `build_fixtures.py` regenerates it byte for byte, and the check enforces that.
- **`check.py`**, plus its output in `check-result.json`.
- **`successor.json`**: sha256 pins for every parent and candidate, plus replacement text for chapter 14 lines 339 and 556. The parent files themselves are untouched.

**How it works**
- **Parity:** the complete Envelope4 value is the only parity source, and its closed schema is unchanged. The embedded copy may differ from the JSON output only by dropping `agentHints` and, by default, `projectRoot`.
- **Renderer gating:** only the 8 HTML commands are accepted, and the checker derives that set from inventory4 and the prototype inventory. Each command has a required, exact `supportedReportViews` list and a fixed set of required and forbidden panels.
- **Panels:** evidence, graph, comparison, history and catalog. Each carries a state: present, omitted, unavailable, corrupt or incompatible, each with a fixed reason list. Three kinds of limit stay separate: limits recorded in the original analysis records, host trimming counts, and browser display limits. Every panel reuses existing records exactly: `CoverageResultV3`, graph `{request, response}` pairs, `comparison:2`, `AnalysisResult` with `FindingSurface`, policy `Rule` and `ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1`. There is no untyped escape hatch.
- **Catalog:** a new private host projection that records its source (plan and policy digest, or a checked registry digest). There is no description text because no admitted source for descriptions exists. Rows grant no permission.
- **History:** only the audit baseline's source Run, requested explicitly. It is never replaced by a later Run.
- **Cross-record joins:** 38 of the cases are misjoins or budget-rule violations, and each must be refused with its own code, so a refusal for the wrong reason fails the check. Examples: graph Run or project mismatch, a hidden continuation page, wrong endpoint or relation, and coverage, comparison, history, plan or registry mismatches. Another 31 cases are shape or depth refusals (for example a non-HTML command, a latest view, an extra envelope field).

**Budgets (UQ-1).** These are development limits, explicitly not measured performance. Each one is recomputed by the checker from the owner schemas and measured record sizes:
- **Panel data limit:** 4 MiB, the accepted codec size.
- **Graph:** 6 slots of 1,000 rows each.
- **Evidence:** 3,956 entries.
- **History:** 1 Run, with up to 5,526 findings.

The prototype's 8 MiB graph cap and 20-run window are not inherited; they appear only as cases in the measurement plan.

The report needs a larger codec than the accepted 4 MiB / depth 32, for two reasons shown by the checker:
- **Size:** only about 5,526 realistic findings fit in 4 MiB, but Envelope4 allows 100,000. An 8,000-finding envelope is refused by the accepted codec and accepted by the report profile. The envelope ceiling is therefore 80 MiB, and the whole document 88,145,920 bytes.
- **Depth:** a policy rule that is valid at depth 32 on its own exceeds 32 once embedded. The report profile allows depth 38.

Required parity is never truncated. An oversized envelope fails required delivery using the existing `DELIVERY` details, and panel data that won't fit is dropped whole, in a fixed order.

- **fit HTML is blocked by an existing gap.** fit declares `candidates` and `evidence-levels` as parity fields, but Envelope4 has no place to carry them for `kind=run`. Until the envelope owner adds one, fit HTML has to fail required delivery (RP-OBL-1). The projection doesn't add a substitute.
- **Changes from the P-5 sketch:**
  - The family name is `opensip.product.report-projection`, matching existing names.
  - History rows are not nested envelopes, which would need an invented request id and termination.
  - Repair-preview reads recipe data from the envelope, with no catalog panel.
- **Remaining obligations:** building the real report and measuring it (RP-OBL-2), registering the schema and codec with the generator (RP-OBL-3), and choosing which graph endpoints the host pre-loads (RP-OBL-4, which affects usefulness only).
- **Arch repo state:** it already had uncommitted changes when I started. None are mine, and every file I relied on is pinned by sha256 and verified by the check.
